title: Why a Still Light Moves in the Dark: The Autokinetic Effect
hook: Why does a single light source seem to drift in complete darkness?

narration.text: Why does a single light source seem to drift in complete darkness?
It is called the autokinetic effect, a strange trick of your brain.
When there are no reference points, your brain struggles to stabilise your gaze.
Tiny, involuntary eye movements are normally corrected by surrounding visual cues.
Without these cues, your brain misinterprets these small movements as the light itself moving.
This can happen when looking at a distant star or a small light in a pitch-black room.
It is a powerful demonstration of how much our perception relies on context.
Have you ever noticed this strange effect yourself?

description: Discover why your eyes play tricks on you in the dark, making a stationary light appear to move. Learn about the autokinetic effect and how our brain interprets visual information without reference points.
topic: Why your eyes play tricks on you in the dark, known as autokinetic effect.
